file_name: Emerald Isle & CourseRev - Quick Chat - 2026/08/06 12:29 PDT - Notes by Gemini

attendees.name: Curtis Baker
attendees.role: Twenty years at Emerald Isle, running the facility day to day and in the process of taking over ownership within about two years; owners John and Holly are above him

pain_points: Their ForeUp POS has stagnated - Curtis said it has not changed its look or added functionality while they have had to build backend workarounds for things like tournament signups, which is driving the switch to TenFore (transcribed as '104') on September 1
Low green fees ('we're only like a 20, 30, you know, at most $40 green fee') leave little room to absorb a per-booking cost
A 55-and-up, price-sensitive clientele that reacts to even a one-dollar rate increase, so any added booking fee has to be handled carefully
Risk that a phone booking fee pushes callers to book on the website instead

After-hours and unanswered calls currently land on a voicemail that is not reliably checked - Curtis said it would be better than 'uh going to a voicemail that probably isn't getting checked on a regular basis'
Past experience that discount promotions get found by regulars who already pay full rate, cancelling out the benefit
current_solution: ForeUp POS and tee sheet, being replaced by TenFore ('104') with a September 1 go-live; hardware already in place and staff training under way. Yealink / RingCentral phone system with calls answered by pro shop staff and no AI vendor evaluated before this ('Um we haven't'). Gallas Golf supplies the Emerald Isle mobile app, with in-house staff for social and graphics, and a self-built Lovable ticketing platform for Curtis's event business. Waitlist will be the native TenFore feature. Tee times are currently booked only a week out.
prospect_questions: How does the AI connect to our current Yealink / RingCentral phone system - do you have your own phone system?
Do you know which provider the Colorado course (Eagle Vail) is moving to?
Do you have a phone vendor you partner with or work well with, or is this completely separate?
How many courses are you at currently, and are you golf only or other types of businesses too?
Is there a point where the caller can get through to a real person?
Does an AI booking show up in a different colour or with a notification that it was booked through the phone service?
Does it book under the caller's existing member account and pull up their information, in real time, with access to the tee sheet?
Do you need access to our ForeUp login to set up the backend?
Is there any flexibility on the $2.50 per booking, or a straight monthly cost, or other ways it can work?
Contract-wise, is it a yearly situation or month to month?
unanswered_questions: When the official CourseRev-TenFore ('104') integration will actually be ready - Bo said 'I'm not sure exactly exactly on the timeline for the official integration with them', hoping for the end of August and no later than the end of September
How the phone-system connection works technically - Bo said 'um the technical specifics I don't know exactly'
How CourseRev gets backend access to the POS - Bo said 'technical specifics. I don't know exactly how we get it set up' and guessed at admin credentials
Which phone provider the Eagle Vail course is switching to - Bo said 'I'm not 100% sure'
The exact number of signed courses - Bo said 'I forget the exact figure' before giving at least 200 signed and roughly 100 live
Exactly how an AI booking will be labelled inside TenFore specifically - Bo said every integration shows in the tee sheet a little differently

objections.trigger_quote: is there any flexibility on that or just a straight monthly cost or, you know, any other ways that that works
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo held the volume-based per-booking model, said CourseRev's pricing is reasonable and that competitors on cheap monthly or yearly subscriptions have AI that does not work well, then proposed that Emerald Isle add the $2.50 to the golfer as a booking fee, saying he does not think twice about a $2-$4 booking fee himself.

objections.trigger_quote: if it was $2 more to book over the phone that they would then they would just go to the website and book it
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo dropped the recommendation of 24/7 coverage and offered a lower-friction entry instead: start on a delayed call forward or after-hours only, and treat the $2.50 as the cost of recovering a $35 booking that would otherwise be missed. He did not return to whether the fee would be passed on to golfers.

objections.trigger_quote: that's all things that I I'll I'll chat with the team
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo accepted the team review and shaped the next steps around it: send the four-to-five minute pre-recorded demo link for Curtis to play at the team meeting the following day, send the agreement for review without expecting a signature, check in by call or text at 2:00 p.m. the next day, and call again the following Monday to see whether a decision had been reached. Curtis's team meeting includes owners John and Holly.

objections.trigger_quote: I don't know if it's worth it to put in the time to set it up for 104 knowing that we're going to switch
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo had offered two contract routes - start now against the existing POS and re-paper for TenFore later, or one agreement naming TenFore with a September 1 effective date. After Curtis said his team would likely want it done in one swoop at the new system, Bo dropped the early-start route himself, saying the extra work was unnecessary and they might as well wait until September 1, and committed to send a single agreement with a September 1 effective date that he would update if the go-live moved.

open.evidence: Curtis was warm and volunteered his own AI enthusiasm - "I'm a big AI guy myself." - describing a ticketing platform he built with Lovable, and said he had already prepared his team for the conversation: "I already kind of planted the seed uh after we chatted".

at_pricing.evidence: Curtis questioned the $2.50 per booking against a low green fee and a price-sensitive membership - "we're in a 55 and up community" - but did not reject it: "So, I don't think it's out of the question." and "I don't think it's a a make it or break it." He handed the decision to his team rather than settling it.

close.evidence: Curtis called the no-commitment terms "a great selling point", accepted the September 1 agreement plan, gave Bo his personal mobile number when asked, and finished with "I think I got enough info um, you know, to to bring it to the table".

No demo course was dialled in this call, so rule 8 does not bite; Eagle Vail and the Torrey Pines / Mission Bay / Balboa group are named as other courses, not as the prospect. Judgement calls: (a) prospect_seniority is 'unknown' because no title is stated anywhere - Curtis has run the facility for 20 years and is buying it within about two years, but owners John and Holly are still above him and he cannot decide alone; (b) meeting_type is 'discovery' although this was the second touch (a phone call the prior week already raised price) and the call also covered pricing and contract terms - no demo was given, so demo_happened is false and features_demoed is empty even though Bo described the product verbally; (c) post_demo sentiment is null for the same reason; (d) the September 1 sequencing objection is coded timing_seasonality but could equally be coded integration, since the timing is driven entirely by the POS migration; (e) the team-approval objection and the second price objection sit inside the same pricing exchange - Curtis's 'that's all things that I I'll I'll chat with the team' was said before Bo's low-friction counter, and the two are modelled separately because Bo answered each with a different move. Speech-to-text artefacts: TenFore appears as '104', 'Tenor', 'Tent for' and 'Tenfor'; ForeUp as 'forup', 'four up', 'FourUp' and 'POSOS'; $2.50 as '250' and '$2.50 50 cent'; Eagle Vail as 'Eagle Veil'; waitlist as 'weight list'; tee time as 'tea time'.
